editorial.thesis: A motor-trade-and-hospitality city of about 135,000. Its retail is heavy on desserts, sweets & ice cream and banks & atms, and thin on fitness & wellness and pharmacy & health retail — and 0% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is about 41% of Mumbai's. 9.64 chain outlets per lakh residents against 23.76 in Mumbai; 9 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by Reliance Smart / Fresh 2, Wellness Forever 2, Raymond 2.

The mapped economy leans to automotive. Shares of all mapped places: automotive 4.9% (Mumbai 2.2%); hotels & stays 8.1% (Mumbai 4.2%); offices 8.5% (Mumbai 14.1%); services & crafts 6.2% (Mumbai 8.1%). Raw counts would mislead because Mumbai is mapped more completely (70,423 places against 1,139), so we compare mix, not counts.
No large under-served zone. No zone combines a large resident base with retail depth below 60% of the city average; the thin spots are small and scattered.

Retail is more concentrated than in Mumbai. 55% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Mumbai 38%). The largest cores are Collectorate · Tilak Memorial (517 places) and MIDC (203).

The widest brand gaps against Mumbai. Café Coffee Day 0 outlets vs 169; Domino's 1 outlets vs 115; Subway 0 outlets vs 81. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 6 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Mumbai, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Collectorate · Tilak Memorial and MIDC are the largest zones by residents (71,000 and 49,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 55% of all commercial places, and Collectorate · Tilak Memorial alone lists 517.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Collectorate · Tilak Memorial holds 6 of the 13 tracked chain outlets, and MIDC adds 4.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Collectorate · Tilak Memorial and MIDC lead on education places (44 and 20, with 16 and 6 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. There is no large amber area. The blue cores include Collectorate · Tilak Memorial.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (70,423 places in Mumbai against 1,139 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Mumbai; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Mumbai, Ratnagiri's mapped places over-index on automotive (4.9% vs 2.2%), hotels & stays (8.1% vs 4.2%), banks & finance (10.2% vs 7.8%) and under-index on offices (8.5% vs 14.1%), services & crafts (6.2% vs 8.1%), food & beverage (9.0% vs 10.1%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 13 outlets of 9 tracked national brands within 6 km — 9.64 per lakh residents against Mumbai's 23.76 (1266 outlets of 44 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Mumbai are Café Coffee Day (0 vs 169); Domino's (1 vs 115); Subway (0 vs 81). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Mumbai's, so low means thin by Mumbai's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 6 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Ratnagiri's age mix against Mumbai: children (0–14) 19.4% vs 19.9%, 15–24 16.8% vs 19.7%, working age 48.8% vs 52.0%, 60+ 15.0% vs 8.4%. Under-25s are 36% of residents.

zones.415612: Reasonably supplied: 517 places for about 71,000 residents (index 113), 6 chain outlets.
zones.415639: Reasonably supplied: 203 places for about 49,000 residents (index 63), 4 chain outlets.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 7.4% of mapped places against 7.0% in Mumbai, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Domino's 1 (Mumbai 115), KFC 1 (Mumbai 38).
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 2.0% of mapped places against 2.7% in Mumbai — below its share.
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 1.7% of mapped places against 1.1% in Mumbai — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Havmor 1 (Mumbai 11). No mapped outlet in either city: Cream Stone.
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 2.3% of mapped places against 1.9% in Mumbai — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Reliance Smart / Fresh 2 (Mumbai 18), DMart 1 (Mumbai 24). No mapped outlet in either city: More, Vishal Mega Mart, Easyday.
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 0.8% of mapped places against 1.3% in Mumbai — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Wellness Forever 2 (Mumbai 17). No mapped outlet in either city: Frank Ross.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 5.5% of mapped places against 4.8% in Mumbai — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Raymond 2 (Mumbai 40), Bata 2 (Mumbai 52), Titan 1 (Mumbai 32). No mapped outlet in either city: Zudio, V-Mart.
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 10.2% of mapped places against 7.8% in Mumbai — above its share.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 2.3% of mapped places against 2.7% in Mumbai — below its share.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 2.3% of mapped places against 4.4% in Mumbai — below its share.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
